title: Transport of bond distances on two and three distinctions under later complete parity rounds
claim: Separate the exact two-attachment comparison for future triples, the several-attachment replacement and any reached counterexample.
standard_statement: Marked minima of connected cuts under exterior growth and preservation by a fixed permutation.
prior_work: The preceding experiment supplies a dense split junction example and a two-terminal transport bound for future pairs.
source_contribution: A lawful shrinking attachment of arbitrarily chosen cost, a hidden equation exposed by the next pair reading at every prescribed current order, a meet-once realization, and a two-attachment endpoint test.

validation.status: Two-law finite replays and independent connected-shore minima, audited analytic parameter family; program referee pending.

completion_gate: Prove each scoped assertion and report unrestricted status.
conclusion: For each fixed r there is a positive-age parity stage preserving every bond distance through r marks and the entire growing end under a renaming, yet the next complete round changes its bond distance on old distinctions. The counterexample also has a realization with at most one shared distinction per ordinary pair of junctions.
claim_scope: All finite reading orders in the complete cheapest-count parity law. Size and junction arity may grow. All examples fail on an old pair after one lawful round.
evidence_class: Constructive counterexample family, conditional transport theorems, and exact finite controls.
unrestricted_open_question: The globally smallest failing stage, how the least sufficient reading order depends on size, and possible sharpness of four marks for two attachments.
